mainTopic: Which שביעית labors are forbidden by the Torah and bring מלקות, and which are only מדרבנן
overview: This amud asks which kinds of farm work in שביעית are forbidden by the Torah itself. The גמרא finishes an answer from before: the Torah forbids the main labors, but not their subcategories (תולדות). The proof is that the Torah lists pruning and grape-picking separately, even though they already fall under sowing and reaping. Listing them shows that only these subcategories carry Torah liability. A ברייתא seems to forbid many other jobs from the words 'your field, not', but the גמרא answers that those bans are only מדרבנן, and the פסוק is just an אסמכתא. On the side, רב עוקבא בר חמא explains that light hoeing to strengthen a tree is forbidden, while light hoeing to seal cracks is allowed. Then רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue whether one who plows in שביעית gets מלקות. The גמרא shows that their argument need not depend on רבי אבין's rule. The 'no מלקות' side can rely on the same extra listing of pruning and grape-picking, and the same ברייתא challenge gets the same מדרבנן answer.

steps.title: The Torah forbids only the main labors, not their subcategories
steps.stepSummary: This finishes an answer already in progress: the subcategories of farm labor are not forbidden by Torah law. The source is the פסוק about שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The subcategories (תולדות) were not forbidden by the Torah, as it is written: 'And in the seventh year shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land; your field you shall not sow, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer begun on the previous lines: the main labors are forbidden by the Torah, but their subcategories are not. Then it quotes the פסוק this is based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא asked how watering a field could be allowed during שביעית. The answer is that watering is only a תולדה, a subcategory, and the Torah did not forbid תולדות. Since the ban on them comes from the רבנן, the רבנן could relax it when there would be a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Subcategories: labors that come from a main labor
'The Merciful One': a name for ה׳, used to mean 'the Torah'
A Sabbath of complete rest
The seventh year, when the land must rest

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The first half, that the main labors (אבות) ARE forbidden by the Torah, came just before this.

phrases.english: The subcategories, the Merciful One did not forbid.
As it is written:
"And in the seventh year, a Sabbath of complete rest
shall be for the land;
your field you shall not sow, etc."
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' covers the rest: don't prune your vineyard, and in the next פסוק, don't reap or pick grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section, about why watering is permitted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between main labors (Torah law) and subcategories (rabbinic law)
steps.terutzMaskana: Subcategories such as watering are only rabbinically forbidden during שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תולדות of farm labor are not forbidden by the Torah during שביעית.

steps.title: Why did the Torah list pruning and grape-picking?
steps.stepSummary: Pruning is already a type of sowing, and grape-picking is already a type of reaping. So why does the Torah name them separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, pruning is included in sowing, and grape-picking is included in reaping. For what law did the Torah write them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the פסוק and asks why it lists pruning and grape-picking when they are already covered. This question sets up the answer that proves the rule from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pruning helps a plant grow, just like sowing, so it is a subcategory of sowing. Grape-picking removes produce from a plant, just like reaping, so it is a subcategory of reaping. If the Torah still names them, the extra mention must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, since...': opens a point everyone agrees on, before a question
Pruning vines
Picking grapes
Included in
For what law? What does this teach?

phrases.english: Now, pruning is included in sowing,
and picking grapes is included in reaping.
For what law
did the Merciful One write them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the פסוק just quoted to pull the rule out of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the Torah naming pruning and grape-picking, when they are already part of sowing and reaping?

steps.title: Only these listed subcategories carry Torah liability
steps.stepSummary: The Torah names them to teach that one is liable for these two subcategories only, and not for any others.
steps.simpleTranslation: To tell you that for these subcategories one is liable, but for the others one is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the Torah named pruning and grape-picking to show they are the only subcategories it forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a few subcategories means the rest are left out. So under Torah law there are four forbidden labors: sowing and pruning, reaping and grape-picking. Every other subcategory, like watering, is forbidden only by the רבנן. This is the source for the rule in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: To say; to teach you
Is liable (to punishment)
The others

steps.whatToRemember: Torah-level שביעית labors: sowing, pruning, reaping and grape-picking. Other subcategories, like watering, are only rabbinic.

phrases.english: To say that for these subcategories one is liable,
but for the others one is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The listing limits Torah liability to these subcategories. Others are not Torah-forbidden.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only pruning and grape-picking, among the תולדות, are forbidden by the Torah.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to forbid every kind of field work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule with a ברייתא. It learns from the פסוק that weeding, hoeing and cutting weeds are also forbidden, because no work at all may be done in your field or vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are they not? But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'Your field you shall not sow, and your vineyard you shall not prune.' From this I would know only sowing and pruning. From where do I know weeding, hoeing and cutting weeds? The פסוק says 'Your field... not,' 'your vineyard... not': no labor at all in your field, and no labor at all in your vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: are other subcategories really not Torah-forbidden? It then brings a ברייתא that seems to forbid many more labors from the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the words 'your field... not' as a general ban on all work in the field and vineyard. That would make weeding, hoeing and cutting weeds Torah-forbidden too. This goes against step 3, which said only the listed subcategories carry Torah liability.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא: brings a source to challenge
Weeding: pulling out weeds
Hoeing: loosening the soil
Cutting weeds or branches without uprooting them
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: And is one not liable? But it was taught:
"Your field you shall not sow,
and your vineyard you shall not prune."
I have only sowing and pruning;
from where do I know weeding, hoeing, and cutting weeds?
The verse says: "Your field... not," "your vineyard... not."
phrases.notes: The ברייתא reads the words 'your field' and 'not' together, as their own ban.

phrases.english: No labor at all that is in your field,
and no labor at all that is in your vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only pruning and grape-picking, among the subcategories, are Torah-forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that weeding, hoeing and cutting weeds are also forbidden. So the Torah seems to forbid all field work, not just the listed subcategories.

steps.title: More tree work is forbidden: pruning, trimming and cutting branches
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: pruning trees, trimming dry branches and cutting big branches are also forbidden, learned from the same words in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that one may not prune, trim dry branches, or cut large branches from a tree? The פסוק says 'your field, not' and 'your vineyard, not', meaning no work at all in your field and no work at all in your vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 4 keeps going. It adds three more tree jobs that are forbidden in שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new job on this list is a subcategory that the Torah never names. The more such jobs the ברייתא forbids, the stronger the challenge becomes against the rule that only זומר and בוצר are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: pruning or trimming a tree
cutting off dry branches
cutting off large branches
a tree
the פסוק teaches us (introduces the source)

phrases.english: From where do we know that one may not prune
and one may not trim dry branches
and one may not cut large branches from a tree?
The verse says: 'Your field, not', 'your vineyard, not'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:4. The ברייתא reads the words 'your field' and 'your vineyard' together with 'not' on their own.

phrases.english: No work at all that is in your field,
and no work at all that is in your vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא that began the challenge in Step 4, adding more forbidden jobs.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from Step 3 that only the two named subcategories are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids tree jobs the Torah does not name, so more than two subcategories are forbidden.

steps.title: Even fertilizing, clearing stones, covering roots and smoking out pests are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds four more forbidden jobs and again learns them from 'your field, not' and 'your vineyard, not'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that one may not fertilize, may not clear away stones, may not cover roots with dust, and may not smoke a tree? The פסוק says 'your field, not' and 'your vineyard, not', meaning no work in your field and no work in your vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second list of forbidden jobs. These jobs care for the soil and the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these jobs is named in the פסוק. Yet the ברייתא still forbids them all from the same words, so the list of forbidden subcategories keeps growing.

keyTerms.meaning: fertilizing with manure
clearing away stones around a tree
covering exposed roots with dust
smoking a tree to kill pests

phrases.english: From where do we know that one may not fertilize
and one may not clear away stones, and one may not cover roots with dust
and one may not smoke out a tree?
The verse says: 'Your field, not', 'your vineyard, not'.
Any work in your field, no,
and any work in your vineyard, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another list to the same ברייתא, making the challenge stronger.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from Step 3 that only two subcategories are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many more unnamed jobs are forbidden from the same words in the פסוק.

steps.title: Maybe even light hoeing and watering are forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises the thought that every job, even light hoeing and filling cracks with water, might be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that one may not hoe lightly under olive trees, may not hoe under vines, may not fill cracks in the ground with water, and may not make small ditches around vines.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible idea (a יכול): since 'all work' is forbidden, maybe even these small jobs are forbidden too. This sets up the limit it will give next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'no work at all' were taken fully, every farm job would be forbidden. The ברייתא now tests whether there is a limit, and these jobs are the test cases.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have thought (introduces an idea that will be rejected)
hoe lightly
hoe or dig
cracks or holes in the ground
small round ditches around the base of a vine

phrases.english: One might think one may not hoe lightly under the olive trees,
and may not hoe under the vines,
and may not fill cracks with water,
and may not make circular ditches for the vines —
phrases.notes: These ditches go around the base of the vine to collect rainwater.

steps.confusionAlert: The word יָכוֹל means 'you might have thought'. It introduces an idea the ברייתא is about to reject, not the final rule.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing forbidden jobs, the ברייתא asks whether the איסור has any limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are light hoeing, watering and making ditches also forbidden under 'no work at all'?

steps.title: The limit: only work like sowing, done in both field and vineyard
steps.stepSummary: Using the words 'your field you shall not sow', the ברייתא compares all work to sowing. Only work done both in a field and in a vineyard is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Your field you shall not sow.' Sowing was already included in the general rule, so why was it named? To compare other jobs to it. Just as sowing is work done in a field and in a vineyard, so too any work done in a field and in a vineyard is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. It uses a היקש to sowing to limit which jobs are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sowing is named even though the general rule already covers it, so it serves as a model. Only jobs that match it, done both in fields and in vineyards, are forbidden. Jobs like light hoeing and watering under vines do not match, so they stay allowed. Even with this limit, the ברייתא still forbids many תולדות, which goes against the rule of Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: it was already included in the general rule
so why was it singled out?
to compare (a היקש), learning one law from another
special, having a defining feature
sowing

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא forbids many farm jobs in שביעית, but only those like sowing, done in both a field and a vineyard. Because it forbids so many subcategories, it challenges the rule that only two are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'it was included in the general rule, so why was it singled out' (זה בכלל ויצא) is a standard way of reading the Torah. A named example becomes a model for the whole category.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'Your field you shall not sow.'
Sowing was included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: The general rule is the line in the same פסוק saying the land must rest in the seventh year.

phrases.english: and why was it singled out?
To compare to it, to tell you:
Just as sowing is special in being
work done in the field and in the vineyard,
so too anything that is
work done in the field and in the vineyard is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יכול of Step 7 by limiting the איסור through a היקש to sowing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only work like sowing, done both in a field and in a vineyard, is forbidden. Light hoeing and watering under vines are allowed.

steps.title: The extra jobs are only Rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the ברייתא. The many extra jobs it listed are forbidden only מדרבנן, and the פסוק it quoted is only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: These other jobs are forbidden only by the רבנן, and the פסוק is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא in Steps 4-8. It says the extra jobs are forbidden only by the רבנן, not by the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to learn many forbidden jobs straight from the פסוק. The גמרא says the Torah itself forbids only the main jobs, such as sowing, pruning, reaping and picking grapes. The other jobs are a Rabbinic rule, and the רבנן 'leaned' it on the פסוק as a hint.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule made by the Rabbis, not written in the Torah itself
A פסוק used only as a hint or support for a Rabbinic rule
Merely, just

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the ברייתא quotes a פסוק for these jobs, they are NOT Torah-level prohibitions. The פסוק is only a support.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the line between Torah-level and Rabbinic-level work in שביעית. That difference matters a lot for the question of מלקות later in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: They are forbidden by Rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the extra jobs the ברייתא listed, apart from the main ones in the פסוק.

phrases.english: and the verse is a mere support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in Steps 4-8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrading the source: the prohibition is Rabbinic, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא learns all these jobs from the פסוק, so they seemed to be Torah prohibitions
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the main jobs are forbidden by the Torah. The rest are Rabbinic, and the פסוק is only a support.

steps.title: Is light hoeing really allowed in the seventh year?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא implied that קשקוש (light hoeing) is allowed. The גמרא challenges this from a פסוק that is explained as forbidding light hoeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is light hoeing allowed in שביעית? But it says, 'The seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow.' 'Let it rest' means from light hoeing, and 'lie fallow' means from clearing stones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks a detail from the ברייתא, which seemed to allow light hoeing. A teaching on a פסוק says that light hoeing is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 7-8 the ברייתא suggested that light hoeing is permitted in שביעית. Here the גמרא brings a teaching that reads the word תשמטנה as forbidding light hoeing. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Light hoeing, loosening the soil around a tree
The seventh year, when the land must rest
'You shall let it rest', read here as forbidding light hoeing
To clear a field of stones

phrases.english: And is light hoeing permitted in the Sabbatical Year?
phrases.notes: This refers back to Steps 7-8, where the ברייתא seemed to allow light hoeing.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"But the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow" —
"You shall let it rest" — from light hoeing,
"and lie fallow" — from clearing stones!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקִשְׁקוּשׁ בִּשְׁבִיעִית מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about a detail of the ברייתא quoted in Steps 7-8
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggestion that light hoeing is permitted in שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching on the פסוק reads תשמטנה as forbidding light hoeing, which contradicts the idea that it is allowed

steps.title: Two kinds of light hoeing
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא explains that there are two kinds of hoeing. Hoeing to strengthen trees is forbidden. Hoeing to seal cracks is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of light hoeing. One strengthens the trees, and one seals cracks in the ground. Strengthening the tree is forbidden. Sealing cracks is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא בר חמא solves the contradiction by splitting light hoeing into two types.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that forbids light hoeing is talking about hoeing that helps the tree grow stronger. The ברייתא that allows it is talking about filling in cracks in the soil. So each source is talking about a different kind of hoeing.

keyTerms.meaning: To strengthen the trees
To seal cracks in the ground
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Light hoeing to strengthen a tree is forbidden in שביעית. Light hoeing to seal cracks is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said:
There are two kinds of light hoeing.
One is to strengthen the trees,
and one is to seal cracks.
Strengthening a tree is forbidden,
sealing cracks is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: תְּרֵי קִשְׁקוּשֵׁי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case into two types (each source speaks about a different kind of hoeing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Light hoeing is one single activity, so it cannot be both forbidden and permitted
steps.terutzMaskana: Hoeing to strengthen the tree is forbidden. Hoeing to seal cracks is permitted.

steps.title: Does one who plows in the seventh year get lashes?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue about someone who plows in שביעית. One says he gets מלקות, and the other says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: about someone who plows in שביעית, רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue. One says he gets lashes, and one says he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a מחלוקת about whether plowing in שביעית carries the punishment of מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing is not one of the jobs written openly in the פסוק. So the question is whether it counts as a Torah לאו that brings מלקות. We are not told which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, which opens a teaching of the אמוראים
One who plows
He receives lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: It was stated: one who plows in the Sabbatical Year,
Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree:
One said: he is flogged,
and one said: he is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section that connects to the theme of forbidden work in שביעית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מחלוקת: one אמורא says one who plows in שביעית gets מלקות, and the other says he does not

steps.title: Suggesting the argument depends on רבי אבין's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the מחלוקת depends on רבי אבין's rule in the name of רבי אילעא. That rule says that when the כלל is a positive command and the פרט is a negative one, we do not use כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about the rule of רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא? He said: wherever a general rule is said as a positive command and a detail as a negative command, we do not learn it with 'general, detail, general'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reason for the מחלוקת. It is setting up the next move, where it will check whether this suggestion really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, כלל ופרט וכלל lets us add more cases that are similar to the detail. רבי אבין says this does not work when the general part is a עשה and the detail is a לאו. The suggestion is that one אמורא accepts this rule, so plowing is not added to the לאו and there is no מלקות. The other אמורא rejects it, so plowing is added and there is מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion that may later be rejected
They disagree
General, detail, general: a method that adds cases similar to the detail
A positive command
A negative command

steps.confusionAlert: לימא is only a suggestion. The גמרא often goes on to reject it, so don't treat it as the final answer yet.

phrases.english: Shall we say that about the rule of Rabbi Avin
in the name of Rabbi Ile'a, they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a:
Wherever a general rule is stated as a positive command
and a detail is stated as a negative command —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ בִּכְלָל וּפְרָט וּכְלָל.
phrases.english: we do not apply to it the method of general, detail, and general.
phrases.notes: This means we can't use the detail to add other similar cases to the negative command.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests what the מחלוקת of Step 12 is based on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis of the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר about מלקות for plowing?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A proposed answer: it depends on whether one accepts רבי אבין's rule that כלל בעשה ופרט בלא תעשה cannot be learned with כלל ופרט וכלל

steps.title: Spelling out how the argument would depend on רבי אבין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its suggestion. The one who gives מלקות rejects רבי אבין's rule, and the one who does not give מלקות accepts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the plower gets מלקות does not accept רבי אבין's rule in the name of רבי אילעא. The one who says he does not get מלקות does accept רבי אבין's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the suggestion it started in the last step. It shows exactly how each side of the מחלוקת would match up with רבי אבין's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you reject רבי אבין's rule, you can use כלל ופרט וכלל to stretch the ban on sowing to cover plowing, so the plower gets מלקות. If you accept the rule, the ban stays limited to sowing alone. Plowing then breaks only the positive command to let the land rest, so there are no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: He is given lashes (מלקות)
He does not hold of it / does not accept it
He holds of it / accepts it

phrases.english: The one who said he is flogged
does not hold of the rule of Rabbi Avin
phrases.notes: So he can use כלל ופרט וכלל: the land must rest, don't sow, a year of rest. That stretches the sowing ban to include plowing.

phrases.english: that he said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a.
And the one who said he is not flogged
holds of the rule of Rabbi Avin.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר לוֹקֶה לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggestion from Step 13 by matching each opinion to a position on רבי אבין's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר really about whether we accept רבי אבין's rule?

steps.title: Everyone rejects רבי אבין's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Both sides may reject רבי אבין's rule. For the one who gives מלקות, that works fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that we do not follow רבי אבין's rule in the name of רבי אילעא. The one who says he gets מלקות is fine with that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that the מחלוקת depends on רבי אבין. It says both sides can reject his rule. Now it must explain the side that says there are no מלקות, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side that gives מלקות has no problem: he uses כלל ופרט וכלל to include plowing. The real question is the other side. If he also rejects רבי אבין's rule, why would he not give מלקות?

keyTerms.meaning: No, that is not right (rejecting the suggestion)
Everyone agrees
Fine, it works well

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא,
phrases.english: that we do not hold of the rule Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a.
The one who said he is flogged — that is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion from Steps 13-14 that the מחלוקת depends on רבי אבין's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole claim that the two opinions split over רבי אבין's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'not flogged' side does not need רבי אבין's rule. He can have a different reason, explained next.

steps.title: Why the other side says no מלקות: only the listed sub-jobs count
steps.stepSummary: The one who says no מלקות points out that the תורה wrote זמירה and בצירה even though they are already part of זריעה and קצירה. That teaches that only these sub-jobs bring מלקות, not other sub-jobs like plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he does not get מלקות can tell you: pruning is already part of sowing, and grape-picking is already part of reaping. So why did the תורה write them separately? To teach that you get מלקות only for these sub-jobs, and not for any other sub-job.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the 'no מלקות' side its own reason, which has nothing to do with רבי אבין. This completes the rejection from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since זמירה is a kind of זריעה and בצירה is a kind of קצירה, the תורה did not need to list them. Listing them shows that only these specific תולדות bring מלקות. Any other תולדה, such as plowing, is left out, so the כלל ופרט וכלל cannot pull it in for מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all (introducing an obvious point)
Pruning vines
Picking grapes
For what law? What does it come to teach?
A sub-job that falls under a main category of work

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר can reject רבי אבין's rule. The one who says there are no מלקות for plowing learns from the extra listing of זמירה and בצירה that only those sub-jobs bring מלקות.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the 'no מלקות' side says plowing is allowed. Plowing is still forbidden in שביעית. The question is only whether it brings מלקות.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה, אָמַר לָךְ:
phrases.english: And the one who said he is not flogged can say to you:
Since pruning is included in sowing,
and grape-picking is included in reaping,
for what law did the Merciful One write them?
To say that for these sub-jobs
one is liable,
but for another sub-job he is not liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה, אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection from Step 15 by giving the 'not flogged' side a reason that does not use רבי אבין's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different source-based reason (extra listing in the פסוק) for the 'not flogged' opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the only way to say 'no מלקות' was to accept רבי אבין's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even without רבי אבין, the extra listing of זמירה and בצירה limits מלקות to those sub-jobs, so plowing brings no מלקות.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids weeding, hoeing and cutting weeds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that other sub-jobs are not included. It quotes a ברייתא that forbids עידור, קשקוש and כיסוח based on the words 'שדך לא' and 'כרמך לא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are other sub-jobs really not included? But a ברייתא teaches: 'Your field you shall not sow and your vineyard you shall not prune.' From this I only know sowing and pruning. From where do we know weeding, hoeing and cutting weeds? The verse says 'your field not', 'your vineyard not': no work at all in your field, and no work at all in your vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 16 by bringing a ברייתא that forbids other sub-jobs too, not just זמירה and בצירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the תורה named זמירה and בצירה to teach that only those sub-jobs are included. But this ברייתא reads the word לא placed right after 'field' and 'vineyard' as a ban on every kind of field and vineyard work. If every job is forbidden, it is hard to say plowing is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? This opens a challenge from a teaching.
Weeding, or digging around plants
Light hoeing, loosening the soil
Cutting away weeds or extra growth
The verse teaches, showing where a rule comes from in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not reading a new verse. It reads the same פסוק in a new way, by focusing on the word לא coming right after 'your field' and 'your vineyard'.

phrases.english: And is that not so? But isn't it taught:
phrases.notes: He means: are other sub-jobs really not included, as step 16 claimed?

phrases.english: "Your field you shall not sow
and your vineyard you shall not prune,"
I only have sowing and pruning.
From where do we know weeding, hoeing, and cutting weeds?
The verse says: "your field, not," "your vineyard, not."
No work of any kind that is in your field,
and no work of any kind that is in your vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in step 16 that only זמירה and בצירה are included.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that the תורה left out other sub-jobs like plowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא reads 'שדך לא, כרמך לא' as a ban on all field and vineyard work, so other sub-jobs seem to be included too.

steps.title: The ברייתא also forbids trimming and cutting tree branches
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: pruning trees, trimming dry branches and cutting large branches are also forbidden, from the same words 'שדך לא, כרמך לא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that one may not prune trees, trim dry branches, or cut large branches from a tree? The verse says 'your field not', 'your vineyard not': any work in your field, no; any work in your vineyard, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds more tree jobs that are forbidden, which makes the challenge from step 17 even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are more sub-jobs that the פסוק does not name outright. The ברייתא uses the same reading of the words to forbid them, so this adds more support to the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Pruning or snipping branches off a tree
Trimming dry branches
Cutting off large branches
A tree

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one may not prune,
and one may not trim dry branches, and one may not cut large branches from a tree?
The verse says: "your field, not," "your vineyard, not":
any work that is in your field, no;
any work that is in your vineyard, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds more forbidden sub-jobs.
steps.raayaObject: That the ban covers more than the jobs named in the פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same ברייתא, reading 'שדך לא, כרמך לא'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that only זמירה and בצירה, among the תולדות, bring מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids more tree work that the פסוק never names, from the same words 'שדך לא, כרמך לא', so more sub-jobs seem to be included.

steps.title: The ברייתא also forbids fertilizing, clearing stones and smoking out pests
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds fertilizing, removing stones from around a tree and fumigating a tree as forbidden, again from 'שדך לא, כרמך לא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that one may not fertilize, may not remove stones, and may not fumigate a tree? The verse says 'your field not', 'your vineyard not': any work in your field, no, and any work in your vineyard, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third group of forbidden jobs, all learned from the same words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these jobs is named in the פסוק. Even so, the ברייתא forbids them from the same words, which shows how wide its reading of 'שדך לא, כרמך לא' really is.

keyTerms.meaning: Fertilizing with manure
Removing stones or extra growth from around a tree
Smoking out (fumigating) a tree to kill worms

phrases.english: From where do we know that one may not fertilize,
and one may not remove stones, and one may not fumigate a tree?
The verse says: "your field, not," "your vineyard, not."
Any work that is in your field, no,
and any work that is in your vineyard, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a third group of forbidden jobs.
steps.raayaObject: That even helper jobs for trees are included in the ban.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same ברייתא, reading 'שדך לא, כרמך לא'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that only זמירה and בצירה, among the תולדות, bring מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fertilizing, removing stones and fumigating are forbidden from the same words in the פסוק, so the ban reaches far beyond the two named sub-jobs.

steps.title: The ברייתא sets a limit: some light jobs are still allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by limiting itself. You might think light hoeing under olive trees and vines, filling cracks with water, and making little water ditches around vines are also forbidden. The full words 'שדך לא תזרע' teach that they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think one may not hoe lightly under olive trees, may not hoe under grapevines, may not fill cracks with water, and may not make little ditches around grapevines. So the verse says: 'Your field you shall not sow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by drawing a line: not every helpful job is forbidden, and some light jobs are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא made the ban very wide. Here it uses the full phrase 'שדך לא תזרע' to hold the ban back, so these light jobs stay allowed. The challenge from step 17 still stands, because many sub-jobs remain forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought, introducing an idea the ברייתא will reject
Cracks or low spots in the ground
Small round ditches around a plant to hold water
Olive trees

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא forbids many sub-jobs from 'שדך לא, כרמך לא,' but it lets some light jobs stay allowed. This ברייתא is now a challenge to the view that only זמירה and בצירה are included.

phrases.english: You might think one may not hoe lightly under the olive trees,
and may not hoe under the grapevines,
and may not fill cracks with water,
and may not make little ditches for the grapevines —
so the verse says: "Your field you shall not sow."
phrases.notes: Reading the full phrase, not just 'your field, not,' narrows the ban, so these light jobs stay allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא by limiting how far its wide ban goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Light hoeing under olive trees and vines, filling cracks with water, and making water ditches around vines are not forbidden, learned from the full words 'שדך לא תזרע'.

steps.title: Sowing is the model for all forbidden work
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why the תורה mentions sowing on its own. It is a model: any work done in both the field and the vineyard is forbidden, just like sowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sowing was already part of the general rule. Why does the תורה mention it separately? To compare other work to it. Just as sowing is work done both in the field and in the vineyard, so too any work done both in the field and in the vineyard is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason behind its list. Sowing is the model, so any work like it, done in both field and vineyard, is forbidden. This completes the challenge against the one who says no מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains step 20: light hoeing and water ditches around vines only help vines, so they are not like sowing and stay permitted. But the main point hurts the one who says no מלקות. The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that many sub-jobs beyond זמירה and בצירה are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: was included in the general rule
was singled out (mentioned on its own)
to compare one thing to another and learn from it
special, has a distinct feature

phrases.english: Sowing was included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: The general rule is the overall ban on working the land in שביעית.

phrases.english: so why was it mentioned on its own?
To compare other work to it,
to tell you:
Just as sowing is special
in being work done in the field and in the vineyard,
so too, anything that is
work done in the field and in the vineyard is forbidden!
phrases.notes: So work done only for vines, like the items in step 20, is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the limit in step 20 and closes the ברייתא's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That many sub-jobs beyond זמירה and בצירה are forbidden from a פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's comparison to זריעה, based on 'שדך לא, כרמך לא'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that other sub-jobs are not included in the prohibition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא learns many forbidden jobs from a פסוק, then זמירה and בצירה are not the only forbidden sub-jobs.

steps.title: Those extra jobs are only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the other jobs in the ברייתא are forbidden only מדרבנן. The פסוק is just an אסמכתא, a hint the חכמים leaned on.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are forbidden only by the חכמים, and the פסוק is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the one who says no מלקות. The ברייתא's list is a rabbinic ban, not a תורה ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that because the ברייתא quotes a פסוק, these jobs are forbidden from the תורה. The answer says the פסוק is only an אסמכתא. So the rule stands that only זמירה and בצירה, as sub-jobs, are forbidden from the תורה and bring מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden by the חכמים, not by the תורה
a פסוק
just a support: a פסוק the חכמים lean on for their own rule, not a real source

steps.whatToRemember: The jobs in the ברייתא (hoeing, fertilizing, removing stones and so on) are forbidden only מדרבנן. From the תורה, only זריעה, זמירה, קצירה and בצירה are forbidden, so only these bring מלקות.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that every time a ברייתא quotes a פסוק, the rule is from the תורה. Sometimes the פסוק is only an אסמכתא for a rabbinic rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the position that there is no מלקות for most work in שביעית, even though many jobs are still forbidden.

phrases.english: These are forbidden only by the rabbis,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in steps 17 to 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the ברייתא's prohibitions as rabbinic, with the פסוק as only an אסמכתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the ברייתא quotes a פסוק, the extra jobs seemed forbidden from the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra jobs are forbidden only מדרבנן, so only the listed sub-jobs bring מלקות.
